ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #20
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. went
   C. goed
   D. goes

2. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the library
   D. Where is the Library

3. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. Only a describing word
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only a joining word

4. When practising Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.

5. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

6. When practising Pronunciation and Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Listening.

7. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.

8. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

9. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.

10. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. quickly
   C. blue
   D. happiness

11. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.

12. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

13. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. No full stops
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

14. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.

15. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Intensive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Intensive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
